cds.title: Smith College Common Data Set 2025-2026 (Google Sheet and PDF in Smith Institutional Research's data folder)

scorecard.title: College Scorecard (location, enrollment, cost; data released 2026-10-15)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class; the file's page headers still read 2024-2025, but its data, file name and questions are for Fall 2025): 8,102 applied, 1,816 admitted (22.4%), 698 enrolled. Residency rows (in-state / out-of-state / international) add up to the totals; international (by address at application) 2,987 applied, 147 admitted, 80 enrolled. Smith is a women's college; the CDS filled the applicant and admit totals in the female row. Waitlist: 1,440 offered a place, 741 accepted, none admitted. Early decision: 1,107 applications and 371 admitted; the CDS lists two ED closing dates (Nov 15 and Jan 5) but gives one count. SAT/ACT submission is optional (29.9% submitted SAT, 14.8% ACT; percentiles cover enrolled students who submitted). The GPA breakdown covers all enrolled students; no average GPA reported (C12 blank). Undergraduate enrollment (2,574) and nonresident (326) are degree-seeking undergraduates from B1/B2 (all undergraduates 2,578; nonresidents 329).

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for 2026-27 from the Common Data Set (G1, G5), confirmed on Smith's Tuition & Aid for Applicants page ('Cost of Attendance, 2026-27'): tuition $70,460, student activities fee $308, food and housing $24,520 (housing $12,300 + food $12,300), books and supplies $800, personal expenses $1,910. Transportation is $708 in the CDS; the page shows $640 (domestic average) and $1,000 (international average). Health insurance of $4,030 is billed too (domestic students may waive); aided international students receive a health grant for it. No total cost of attendance is printed, so none is shown. Per-credit charge $2,200. Aid: CDS H6 says need-based and non-need-based institutional aid is available to nonresident degree-seeking undergraduates; 155 received it, average about $89,103 (the CDS reports this table for 2025-26 estimated).
